accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 8 and Theorem 9
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The efficient-estimation and simultaneous-inference claims are conditional on foldwise R_Sigma=o_P(1) and Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2); constructing such a coherent fit remains OEQ 2.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Efficient cross-fitted inference conditional on the displayed coherent nuisance-rate conditions, rather than an unconditional implementability claim.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 2, lines 229–238; Theorem 4, lines 265–277; Supplement S8.2, lines 1027–1129
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes the binary observed tangent space and gives a closed-form binary influence function; for continuous Y it states that a closed-form EIF is generally unavailable and proposes a basis-function approximation.

Appendix A.8 extends the framework to K>2, assumes each feature moment matrix is nonsingular, constructs inverse-feature products and a valid influence function, and gives strict modal/ordinal label-alignment conditions; it does not state uniform singular-value or modal-margin lower bounds.
The paper compares bridge and array-decomposition restrictions, describes three-view array recovery, and distinguishes ordinal label recovery from hidden-confounder identification.
The article identifies a class of nonclassical nonlinear errors-in-variables models through an eigenvalue–eigenfunction decomposition and a labeling/indexing condition.
The paper develops nonparametric causal identification with three jointly conditionally independent proxies and builds on Hu–Schennach recovery.
Kruskal-rank conditions identify a three-view finite latent-class model up to simultaneous label swapping.

Make OEQ 2 operational by naming a smoothness class, sieve dimension schedule, label-selection criterion, and rates sufficient for every coordinate of R_Sigma and Delta_n.
